content.text: {"query":"SF Bay Area office rent and vacancy trends 2021-2026 by submarket (SF CBD, SOMA, Peninsula, Oakland) including effective rents and concessions","summary":"From 2021–mid‑2026 the Bay Area office market moved from pandemic‑era distress toward selective recovery, but performance varied by submarket. San Francisco CBD/SOMA saw the largest swings: vacancy peaked in 2023–2024 (mid‑30%s total vacancy) and began declining through 2025–Q1 2026 as leasing momentum returned, particularly into high‑quality, move‑in‑ready space; asking rents stabilized and began rising modestly while effective (net) rents lagged because landlords continued to offer large concessions (extended free‑rent months and elevated TI allowances). CBRE, JLL and Cushman reports show San Francisco overall vacancy in the low‑to‑mid 30s% at end‑2025 with asking rents in the high $60s–$70s/SF (annual gross) but materially lower effective rents after concessions. ([cbre.com](https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/san-francisco-office-snapshot-q4-2025?utm_source=openai))\n\nSuburban/submarket contrasts: Peninsula/Silicon Valley saw elevated vacancy in 2021–2022 but stronger leasing and faster vacancy improvement into 2025–Q2 2026, with Kidder Mathews and JLL reporting lower vacancy than core SF and asking rents remaining relatively resilient (monthly ~$5.50/PSF reported for Peninsula direct asking in Q2 2026) though effective‑rent discounts and concession packages (free rent, TI) were still prevalent. Oakland’s office market improved more recently: Colliers Q1 2026 notes vacancy falling to ~19–20% and landlords increasing concession intensity to compete for tenants. Industry analyses (CBRE Econometric Advisors, Colliers, JLL) consistently report rising concession levels since 2021 and that effective rents across Bay Area submarkets are meaningfully below headline asking rents due to larger free‑rent periods and TI allowances. ([kidder.com](https://kidder.com/market-reports/peninsula-office-market-report/?utm_source=openai))"}
